title: Growing the mesh
question: Does it scale, and where is the edge?

headlines.label: nodes on the default router profile, at full delivery
headlines.detail: 100% to HQ, 100% back; ready 2 s after power-on

headlines.label: delivered past the edge (144 nodes)
headlines.detail: a full routing table triggers an advert storm

headlines.label: jump in control traffic one step past the edge

summary: Square grids from 25 to 144 radios, every node streaming to HQ and HQ streaming back. Up to 128 nodes the mesh scales as it should: delivery stays at 99% or better both ways, every node has a route to HQ within 2 s of power-on, and each node's control traffic grows in step with the mesh. The default router profile remembers 128 other nodes, and past that the mesh doesn't degrade gracefully. Routers start evicting nodes and hearing them again a moment later. Each re-learned node counts as new and resets that router to its fastest advertising rate; with every router churning, all of them are pinned there, so control traffic jumps 6x and delivery falls to 36%. The default profile is therefore a hard ceiling. A larger mesh needs the host profile (4,096 nodes) on every router, and the storm itself is worth fixing in the router.

series.name: every node has a route to HQ

method: The real wayfinder router (default capacity profile) on square grids, 450 m apart, one shared 2.4 GHz channel at 24 dBm with a 700 m range. Adverts run on a 1–10 s schedule. After 60 s of warm-up, every node streams to HQ and HQ to every node at 0.5 packets/s for 60 s. Reachability is delivered packets; convergence is the first instant every node held a route to HQ, sampled every 0.5 s.
